answer: An agent market requires every voting identity to lock a $100 bond for 90 days before its vote counts. An attacker can mirror an agent a thousand times, but activating those copies ties up $100,000 for three months, making influence costly even if identities are free. Like a vine that must spend resources to reach nectar, each added identity demands more capital. This limits cheap swarms, though a wealthy attacker can still buy influence.
